summary: An 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena for the Golden State Warriors (NBA) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025), anchoring an 11-acre, privately financed mixed-use development in Mission Bay with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space (leased in full by Uber as its San Francisco headquarters since 2022), 100,000 sq ft of retail ("Thrive City") and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza; designed by MANICA Architecture with Gensler (interiors), built by a Mortenson/Clark Construction joint venture, and opened September 6, 2019.

milestones.text: Golden State Warriors ownership purchases the ~12-acre former Salesforce.com site in Mission Bay
Chase Center opens; the Warriors begin play there
Chase Center achieves LEED Gold certification (Building Design and Construction: New Construction), one of few major US sports venues to do so
Uber occupies the adjacent Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (1655 & 1725 3rd St) as its San Francisco/global headquarters, on a 20-year lease covering ~584,000-586,000 sq ft for ~4,000 employees

SF Board of Supervisors approves a separate, Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex (129-room hotel, 21 condos, ~25,000 sf retail) on adjacent Blocks 29-30 near Chase Center; as of the most recent reporting found (~Feb 2025), construction had not begun. Its relationship to this parcel (8722025) is not confirmed -- see open questions. Not treated as this record's own status: Chase Center itself opened in 2019 and remains complete regardless of this separate, unconfirmed, unbuilt proposal.
Golden State Valkyries (WNBA expansion team) play their inaugural regular-season home game at Chase Center, vs. the Los Angeles Sparks

California Superior Court upholds the subsequent Environmental Impact Report certified by OCII for the Warriors Arena Project, in litigation filed by the Mission Bay Alliance against OCII, the City and others

OCII Commission adopts Resolution No. 14-2026, approving a Sixth Amendment to the Mission Bay South Signage Master Plan that increases character heights and awning-sign flexibility for mixed-use retail and for the Event Center Sign Program at the Warriors event center on Blocks 29-32 (adopted 4-0 with one absence)

LEED Gold (Building Design and Construction: New Construction), achieved about a year after opening; also GBAC STAR facility accreditation

Uber occupies the entire office component (Mission Bay 3 & 4 towers, 1655 & 1725 3rd St) as its San Francisco/global headquarters: ~584,000-586,000 sq ft, 20-year lease, ~4,000 employees, 145 dedicated parking spaces
Named under a naming-rights deal with JPMorgan Chase
Golden State Warriors (NBA, since 2019) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025)

As of July 2016, OCII expected the Golden State Warriors to return to the Commission in coming months for approval of a comprehensive signage package, with an accompanying update on SBE, local hire, art and design

Port Commission agenda of May 9, 2023 included proposed License 17036 with GSW Arena, LLC, for white, yellow and metered parking spaces on game and special event dates located in and around Chase Center

open_questions: 2026-09-23: this record's geometry was migrated off status.csv (record_id changed from the blklot '8722025' to 'mission_bay_chase_center') because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 towers byte-identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The new geometry is the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OSM building footprints subtracted out -- see the geojson's own digitization_method. Two small structures inside the resulting polygon are not yet identified: an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others not yet checked against a satellite pass.

Chase Center's final cost is genuinely disputed in reporting: $1.4B is the most-repeated figure (Construction Dive), but a Warriors executive (Rick Welts, per Wikipedia) put the actual final cost closer to $1.3B after a roughly 30% overrun from an original budget. A separate 2019 Construction Dive piece on the (distinct, unbuilt) hotel/condo proposal used '$1.5B Chase Center' in its own headline, which appears to conflate the arena with that proposal; that figure is not used here.
Uber's exact current headcount or lease status as of 2026 was not independently verified; the source describing its 584,000-586,000 sq ft lease is from January 2022.

The Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex on adjacent Blocks 29-30 is financially and physically tied to Chase Center but may sit on a separate parcel; whether it falls within blklot 8722025 or is a distinct, not-yet-built record is not confirmed. Current 2026 construction status is also unconfirmed.

No primary Port of San Francisco or OCII page dedicated specifically to Chase Center was found (as a privately financed project, it may not have one); the only agency-level source found was SFPUC/CleanPowerSF's sustainability write-up.
No openly licensed image was found; recommend linking rather than hosting until one is confirmed.
